facts.statement: Huabeisaurus was a sauropod dinosaur that lived in northern China during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 99.7 to 70.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Huabeisaurus (, meaning "North China lizard") was a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian to Maastrichtian stages, around 99.7–70.6 million years ago) of what is present-day northern China.

facts.statement: The species Huabeisaurus allocotus was first described by Pang Qiqing and Cheng Zhengwu in 2000.
facts.quote: The type species, Huabeisaurus allocotus, was first described by Pang Qiqing and Cheng Zhengwu in 2000.

facts.statement: Numerous remains of Huabeisaurus, including teeth, partial limbs, and vertebrae, were found in the 1990s.
facts.quote: It is known from numerous remains found in the 1990s, which include teeth, partial limbs and vertebrae.

facts.statement: Fossils of Huabeisaurus were discovered at Kangdailiang and Houyu in Zhaojiagou Town, Tianzhen County, Shanxi province, China.
facts.quote: Huabeisaurus comes from Kangdailiang and Houyu, Zhaojiagou Town, Tianzhen County, Shanxi province, China.

facts.statement: The holotype was found in the upper member of the Huiquanpu Formation, dated to the Late Cretaceous based on ostracods, charophytes, and fission-track dating.
facts.quote: The holotype was found in the unnamed upper member of the Huiquanpu Formation, which is Late Cretaceous (?Cenomanian–?Campanian) in age based on ostracods, charophytes, and fission-track dating.

facts.statement: Huabeisaurus was estimated to be 20 meters long and 5 meters high.
facts.quote: Huabeisaurus measures 20 m long and 5 m high, as estimated by Pang and Cheng in 2000.

facts.statement: A set of 12 characters identified by D'Emic et al. in 2013 differentiate Huabeisaurus from other sauropods.
facts.quote: A set of 12 characters were identified by D'Emic et al. in 2013 that differentiate Huabeisaurus from other sauropods.

facts.statement: An isolated humerus designated as the paratype was found over 200 meters from the type locality in a fluvially deposited sandy conglomeratic layer of the lower Huiquanpu Formation.
facts.quote: An isolated humerus, designated the paratype by Pang and Cheng, comes from a locality over 200 m away from the type locality of Huabeisaurus, in a fluvially deposited sandy conglomeratic layer in the lower member of the Huiquanpu Formation.

facts.statement: The discoverers erected the family Huabeisauridae for the genus, though this name is not widely used by paleontologists.
facts.quote: The discoverers erected a new family for the genus, Huabeisauridae, although this family name is not widely used amongst paleontologists.

facts.statement: D'Emic et al. recently proposed the family Huabeisauridae again because the family Euhelopodidae, to which Huabeisaurus is most recently assigned, may need to be split into smaller clades.
facts.quote: Recently, the family was again proposed, this time by D'Emic et al. because Euhelopodidae, which Huabeisaurus has been assigned to most recently, might have to be split into smaller clades throughout Somphospondyli because of all the taxa assigned to it.

facts.statement: Huabeisaurus measured 20 meters in total length, making it large compared to most dinosaurs but only midsized by sauropod standards.
facts.quote: Measuring 20 m in total length, Huabeisaurus is large when compared to most dinosaurs, but by sauropod standards, it was only midsized.

facts.statement: The absence of sutures on the vertebrae suggests the specimen was nearing sexual maturity, while open sutures on the scapula and ilium suggest it had not reached full maturity.
facts.quote: The absence of sutures between the neural arches and centra of cervical, dorsal, and caudal vertebrae suggests that the specimen was nearing sexual maturity, but the open sutures between the scapula and coracoid, and the ilium and some sacral ribs suggest that it had not reached full maturity.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen originally contained 32 caudal vertebrae before some were lost during fossilization or collection.
facts.quote: Twenty-seven caudal vertebrae are shown on the quarry map, but 30 were found in the collection, and pre-restoration photos indicate that 32 were originally present.

facts.statement: Two well-preserved teeth with wrinkled enamel are attributed to the holotype individual of Huabeisaurus.
facts.quote: The teeth are attributed to the holotype individual based on their close association with other bones and lack of evidence for transport from another site.

facts.statement: Pre-restoration photographs reveal that the sacrum of Huabeisaurus consisted of at least six vertebrae.
facts.quote: The sacrum is currently heavily restored with plaster, but pre-restoration photographs show the sacrum in two oblique dorsal views and right lateral view.

facts.statement: It is debated whether a seventh sacral vertebra existed in Huabeisaurus, as the ribs of the candidate vertebra cannot be verified.
facts.quote: The first vertebra crushed into the sacrum could represent a seventh sacral vertebra; because the ribs of this dorsal vertebra are not observable firsthand or in photographs, but it cannot be verified whether or not these ribs contacted the ilium.

facts.statement: Twelve chevrons are currently preserved in the Huabeisaurus holotype, covering nearly the entire length of the caudal vertebral series.
facts.quote: Eleven chevrons were listed in the holotype of Huabeisaurus by Pang and Cheng, but thirteen are visible in pre-reconstruction photographs, and twelve are currently present in the Museum of Shijiazhuang University.

facts.statement: The scapula blade of Huabeisaurus shows acromion development and distal expansion similar to other somphospondylans but less pronounced than in rebbachisaurids.
facts.quote: The development of the acromion and distal expansion of the blade are similar to those of other somphospondylans and not as marked as in rebbachisaurids.

facts.statement: The Huabeisaurus radius shaft changes from an oval cross-section at the top to a rounded D-shape at the mid-shaft.
facts.quote: The oval cross-section of the upper shaft gradually transforms into a rounded D-shape at mid-shaft, with the long axis of the cross section extending transversely.

facts.statement: The cervical ribs of Huabeisaurus hang down (pendant) to a depth roughly equal to the height of the vertebra, a trait shared with other East Asian Cretaceous sauropods.
facts.quote: The cervical ribs are pendant, extending ventrally for a distance subequal to the height of the centrum, as in several other East Asian Cretaceous sauropods.

facts.statement: The original description of Huabeisaurus proposed five sacral vertebrae based on rib and foramen counts, though later evidence suggests at least six.
facts.quote: The original description of Huabeisaurus suggested that only five sacral vertebrae were present based on the number of sacral ribs and intercostal foramina.

facts.statement: Huabeisaurus was originally described in the year 2000.
facts.quote: Since 2000, the year of the original description of Huabeisaurus, 17 new sauropod species have been erected from the Cretaceous of East Asia.

facts.statement: Researchers erected the family Huabeisauridae to include Huabeisaurus and the closely related Tangvayosaurus.
facts.quote: A new family was erected to place Huabeisaurus in, along with the closely related Tangvayosaurus. The family was named Huabeisauridae.

facts.statement: Recent studies suggest that Huabeisaurus belongs to the family Euhelopodidae.
facts.quote: Finally, it has recently been suggested by D'emic et al. that Huabeisaurus is a member of Euhelopodidae.

facts.statement: Huabeisaurus is classified within the family Saltasauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Saltasauridae

facts.statement: Huabeisaurus is placed in the subfamily Opisthocoelicaudiinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Opisthocoelicaudiinae

facts.statement: The genus Huabeisaurus was named by Pang and Cheng in 2000.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Pang & Cheng, 2000

facts.statement: The species Huabeisaurus allocotus was named by Pang and Cheng in 2000.
facts.quote: species_authority: Pang & Cheng, 2000

facts.statement: Amphicoelicaudia allocata is a synonym of Huabeisaurus allocotus.
facts.quote: synonyms: Amphicoelicaudia allocata Cheng, et al., 1994

facts.statement: Huabeisaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 75 to 72 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 75 y 72 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Fossils of Huabeisaurus have been found in Kangdailiang and Houyu, Zhaojiagou Town, Tianzhen County, Shanxi province, China.
facts.quote: Huabeisaurus comes from Kangdailiang and Houyu, Zhaojiagou Town, Tianzhen County, Shanxi province, China.

facts.statement: The holotype of Huabeisaurus was found in the upper member of the Huiquanpu Formation, dated to the Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian to Campanian) using ostracods, charophytes, and fission-track dating.
facts.quote: The holotype was found in the unnamed upper member of the Huiquanpu Formation, which is Late Cretaceous (?Cenomanian–?Campanian) in age based on ostracods, charophytes, and fission-track dating.

facts.statement: Huabeisaurus is known from teeth and most of the postcranial skeleton.
facts.quote: El saurópodo titanosauriforme del Cretáceo tardío Huabeisaurus se conoce por los dientes y gran parte del esqueleto poscraneal.

facts.statement: Huabeisaurus reached a total length of 20 meters, which is large compared to most dinosaurs but only medium-sized among sauropods.
facts.quote: Con una longitud total de 20 metros, el Huabeisaurus es grande en comparación con la mayoría de los dinosaurios, pero según los estándares de saurópodos, solo era de tamaño mediano.

facts.statement: Huabeisaurus had a hip height of 5 meters.
facts.quote: Tenía una altura de cadera de 5 metros.

facts.statement: Huabeisaurus was a quadrupedal herbivore with a long neck and tail, like other sauropods.
facts.quote: Como otros saurópodos, habría sido un herbívoro cuadrúpedo con un largo cuello y cola.

facts.statement: Researchers suppose the Huabeisaurus skeleton belonged to an almost mature individual.
facts.quote: Se ha supuesto que el esqueleto pertenecía a un individuo casi maduro.

facts.statement: D'Emic et al. (2013) identified several unique features of Huabeisaurus, including divided vertebral laminae, specific caudal rib patterns, a coracoid with a tubercle, and a high tibia-to-femur ratio.
facts.quote: According to D'Emic et al. (2013) Huabeisaurus can be distinguished based on this set of autapomorphies: the division of some presacral vertebral laminae; posterior cervical vertebrae with a divided prezygodiapophyseal lamina; anterior dorsal vertebrae with a divided anterior spinodiapophyseal lamina; the presence of postzygapophyseal spinodiapophyseal fossa that are larger than postzygapophyseal centrodiapophyseal fossa on anterior-middle caudal vertebrae; caudal vertebrae with small caudal ribs that disappear around caudal vertebra eight; ventrally one-third of anterior-middle caudal vertebral centra expanded posteriorly; two longitudinal ridges on the lateral faces of mid-caudal vertebral centra; a coracoid with tubercle near anterodorsal edge of lateral face; the distal end of radius about twice as broad transversely as midshaft (convergently acquired in derived titanosaurs); a tubercle on ischial plate that projects from posterior margin; the development of fossae relative to one another in caudal vertebral neural arches; and a high tibia-to-femur ratio.

facts.statement: The geological horizon containing an isolated Huabeisaurus humerus also yielded hadrosaurid specimens and indeterminate ankylosaurid material.
facts.quote: The horizon that yielded the humerus also contains hadrosaurid specimens referred to cf. Shantungosaurus sp. and indeterminate ankylosaurid material.

facts.statement: The type locality of Huabeisaurus has also produced the ankylosaur Tianzhenosaurus and theropod material referred to cf. Szechuanosaurus campi.
facts.quote: This locality has also produced the ankylosaur Tianzhenosaurus, theropod material referred to cf. Szechuanosaurus campi (now regarded as a nomen dubium), and indeterminate hadrosaurid material.

facts.statement: It remains uncertain how long the endemism of East Asian sauropods, including Huabeisaurus, lasted.
facts.quote: Both earlier and later analyses suggest some degree of endemism in East Asia, though its temporal duration remains uncertain.

facts.statement: Pang and Cheng tentatively suggested that Titanosaurus falloti belongs to Huabeisaurus, but this is disputed because the femur lacks uniquely shared features.
facts.quote: Pang and Cheng tentatively suggested that "Titanosaurus" falloti be referred to Huabeisaurus. However, "T." falloti is only represented by femoral remains, and its femur bears no uniquely shared features with Huabeisaurus.

facts.statement: Two well-preserved teeth were recovered from the holotype, one found in the quarry and a second discovered during field sample preparation at Shijiazhuang University.
facts.quote: Se conservaron dos dientes. Se descubrió un diente en la cantera durante la excavación y se encontró un segundo al abrirse los bochones de campo durante la preparación del espécimen en la Universidad de Shijiazhuang.

facts.statement: The tooth crowns are subcylindrical with slenderness indices of 3.46 and 3.36, which are slightly thinner than originally described by Pang and Cheng and intermediate between wide and narrow-crowned sauropods like Euhelopus and Phuwiangosaurus.
facts.quote: Las coronas son subcilíndricas, con índices de esbeltez de 3,46 y 3,36, que son ligeramente más delgadas que lo descrito originalmente por Pang y Cheng e intermedias en esbeltez entre saurópodos de corona ancha y estrecha, por ejemplo, Euhelopus y Phuwiangosaurus.

facts.statement: Neither of the teeth is strongly twisted along its length, unlike the upper teeth of brachiosaurids.
facts.quote: Ninguno de los dientes está fuertemente torcido a lo largo de su longitud como en los dientes superiores de los braquiosáuridos.

facts.statement: Four cervical vertebrae were recovered from the holotype quarry site, consisting of two fragmentary and two nearly complete specimens.
facts.quote: Se recuperaron un total de cuatro vértebras cervicales de la cantera holotípica. Dos de ellas son fragmentarias, mientras que las otras dos vértebras están casi completas.

facts.statement: An almost complete sacrum composed of six vertebrae was recovered from the quarry, originally lacking only some ribs.
facts.quote: Un sacro casi completo que consta de seis vértebras se recuperó de la cantera, originalmente solo carecía de algunas costillas.

facts.statement: The cervical ribs are hanging and extend ventrally for a distance less than the height of the centrum, a trait shared with various other Cretaceous sauropods from East Asia.
facts.quote: Las costillas cervicales están colgantes y se extienden ventralmente por una distancia inferior a la altura del centro, como en varios otros saurópodos cretáceos de Asia oriental.

facts.statement: According to D'Emic et al. in 2013, Huabeisaurus is distinguished by a unique set of autapomorphies including divided presacral vertebral laminae, divided prezygodiapophyseal laminae in posterior cervical vertebrae, divided anterior spinodiapophyseal laminae in anterior dorsal vertebrae, a larger postzygapophyseal spinodiapophyseal fossa than the postzygapophyseal centrodiapophyseal fossa in anterior and middle caudal vertebrae, small caudal ribs disappearing around the eighth caudal vertebra, posterior expansion of the anterior and middle caudal vertebral centra by one-third, two longitudinal crests on the lateral faces of the mid-caudal vertebral centra, a coracoid with a tubercle near the anterodorsal edge of the lateral face, a distal radius approximately twice as wide transversely as the mid-shaft, a tubercle on the ischial plate projecting from the posterior margin, relative fossae development in caudal neural arches, and a high tibia-to-femur ratio.
facts.quote: Según D'Emic et al. en 2013 Huabeisaurus se puede distinguir basándose en este conjunto de autapomorfías, la división de algunas láminas vertebrales presacras, vértebras cervicales posteriores con una lámina prezigodiapofisaria dividida, vértebras dorsales anteriores con una lámina espinodiapofisaria anterior dividida, la presencia de fosa espinodiapofisaria postzygapofiseal que es más grande que la fosa centrodiapofisaria postzygapofiseal en vértebras caudales anteriores y medias, vértebras caudales con pequeñas costillas caudales que desaparecen alrededor de la vértebra caudal ocho, ventralmente, un tercio de los centros vertebrales caudales anteriores y medios se expandió posteriormente, dos crestas longitudinales en las caras laterales de los centros vertebrales de la mitad del caudal, un coracoide con tubérculo cerca del borde anterodorsal de la cara lateral, el extremo distal del radio aproximadamente dos veces más ancho transversalmente que el eje medio, adquirido de manera convergente en titanosaurios derivados, un tubérculo en placa isquial que se proyecta desde el margen posterior; el desarrollo de fosas relativas entre sí en los arcos neurales vertebrales caudales; y una alta proporción de tibia a fémur.

facts.statement: Due to its relative integrity, Huabeisaurus represents a significant taxon for understanding the evolution of sauropods in Asia.
facts.quote: Debido a su relativa integridad, Huabeisaurus representa un taxón significativo para comprender la evolución de los saurópodos en Asia.

facts.quote: Los descubridores han propuesto una nueva familia para este género, Huabeisauridae, pero esto no es compartido por la mayoría de los paleontólogos aún.
